events.continuity_hook: The hotel choice is settled, but the reservation currently ends one night too early for the fixed work schedule and return flight.
events.interaction_goal: Extend the existing reservation through Thursday checkout, retain the quoted nightly terms if available, and obtain a corrected four-night confirmation.
events.scenario_brief: After Avery reserves the walkable New Orleans hotel, the confirmation shows checkout on Wednesday even though her booked return flight leaves Thursday afternoon and the Thursday morning inspection requires a fourth night. The property still shows the same room available for Wednesday night, but the confirmation must be corrected before the advance-payment date.

events.continuity_hook: The vacation dates and shared-room arrangement are established, while the destination, driving schedule, and lodging area remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the three coastal destinations using realistic driving times and current six-night lodging availability, then narrow the trip to one island and a practical arrival plan.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife begin planning a six-night September coastal vacation from Saturday through Friday. Amelia Island, Jekyll Island, and Tybee Island are all reachable by car from Atlanta, but they differ in drive time, the concentration of hotels directly by the ocean, and the availability of rooms with private balconies for the full stay.

events.continuity_hook: The destination, dates, and travel mode are fixed, leaving the exact beachfront area and hotel shortlist to determine.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm which hotels provide direct beach access, distinguish private ocean-view balconies from generic balcony listings, and create a shortlist with complete six-night costs.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife choose Amelia Island and plan to drive from Atlanta on Saturday morning. Several properties have rooms for all six nights, but some are across a main road from the beach, while two oceanfront options list balcony rooms with different view descriptions, parking charges, and cancellation dates.

events.continuity_hook: Avery has a focused oceanfront shortlist, but the quoted totals are not directly comparable because the included items, fees, deposits, and cancellation terms differ.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate comparable totals for one room and two adults, separate refundable deposits from actual charges, verify the balcony categories, and identify the stronger booking option.
events.scenario_brief: Two Amelia Island hotels remain viable for the six-night stay. One offers a higher-floor partial-ocean-view balcony and includes breakfast but adds nightly parking; the other has a lower total room charge and a direct-ocean-view balcony but adds a resort fee and requires a larger deposit. Their cancellation deadlines fall on different days.

events.continuity_hook: The leading rate no longer provides one room category for the whole vacation, forcing a choice between moving rooms mid-stay and paying more for an uninterrupted stay.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the split-room arrangement with the continuous six-night option, confirm whether the property handles luggage during the room move, and decide which stay to book.
events.scenario_brief: Before Avery books, the direct-ocean-view room at the lower-priced hotel becomes unavailable for the first two nights. That property can offer a standard room followed by an in-stay move to the balcony room, while the other shortlisted hotel still has its partial-ocean-view balcony category for all six nights at the earlier quote.

events.continuity_hook: The hotel and room category are selected; booking details and the road-trip arrival estimate are the remaining administrative steps.
events.interaction_goal: Reserve the selected room for both travelers, record a realistic arrival window, verify the complete charge and cancellation deadline, and produce the confirmed drive-and-hotel itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife choose the uninterrupted six-night balcony stay and are ready to reserve it. Their planned Saturday drive should reach Amelia Island in midafternoon, but the rate requires arrival by 6:00 p.m. unless the hotel records a later arrival, and the final confirmation must include both adults, parking, and the Friday checkout date.
